title: `validateStep2 = () => true` — 67% risk reduction with no justification or residual documentation
description: `validateStep2` unconditionally returns `true`. Users can claim any residual risk score (e.g., 67% reduction) with zero documentation, justification, or treatment rationale. Risk assessment results are not reproducible or comparable. ISO 27001 Clause 6.1.2(d) requires documented, repeatable criteria. An auditor cannot verify any residual risk score in the system — immediate Stage 2 non-conformity.
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27: `validateStep2` itself now only checks `impactAreas.length`, but the original intent (require documented rationale when a large risk reduction is claimed) was relocated to `validateStep3`: `if (residualRiskScore < inherentRiskScore * 0.4 && !formData.treatmentDescription?.trim()) newErrors.treatmentDescription = '...'` — i.e. >60% reduction now requires `treatmentDescription` (not `residualNotes`, and 60% not the original 50% threshold). The UI hint at line ~2525 (`riskReduction > 60`) is consistent with this. This is a legitimate re-implementation, not a broken fix — still open/blocking behavior verified absent.

title: Authority matrix (`RISK_LEVELS.minLevel`) defined in code but approver dropdown completely unfiltered — manager-level user can approve Critical risk
description: `RISK_LEVELS.minLevel` authority matrix is defined in code but the approver dropdown is populated from all org users without filtering to the required authority tier. A manager can approve a Critical risk that requires director-level sign-off. Formal risk governance is legally invalid. All existing Critical risk acceptances may have the wrong authorisation tier. ISO 27001 Annex A 5.2 requires defined risk ownership and acceptance authority at the appropriate level.
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27 against vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/risk-register/RiskAcceptanceWorkflow.jsx:698-703: `RISK_LEVEL_AUTHORITY` maps risk level to a minimum `AUTHORITY_RANK`, and `eligibleApprovers = approvers.filter(u => (AUTHORITY_RANK[u.role?.toLowerCase()] ?? 0) >= requiredRank)` genuinely filters the approver list before rendering. Confirmed fixed.

title: ReferenceError: `projectId` is referenced but never defined/destructured in AcceptanceRequestForm and ApprovalDecisionForm — crashes the acceptance workflow UI on render
description: `AcceptanceRequestForm` destructures its props as `{ acceptance, onChange, onSubmit, isSubmitting, readOnly = false, approvers = [] }` (no `projectId`), yet its JSX at line 232 reads `<PermissionHide permission="risk.update" allowProjectGrant projectId={projectId}>` — `projectId` is not a prop, a local variable, or an import anywhere in this component's scope. Same defect independently in `ApprovalDecisionForm` (props destructured at line 255-260, `projectId` referenced at lines 316 and 328). This throws a genuine `ReferenceError: projectId is not defined` at render time, crashing the enclosing tree. Verified by direct code inspection, not by executing the app.

title: `approvers` prop hardcoded to `[]` at both real render call sites of RiskAcceptanceWorkflow — no risk acceptance request can ever be submitted
description: Both live call sites that render `<RiskAcceptanceWorkflow>` (RiskRegisterPageDrawer.jsx and RiskRegisterDrawer.jsx) pass `approvers={[]}` literally. Since `AcceptanceRequestForm`'s approver `<Select>` is populated entirely from the `approvers` prop, the dropdown is always empty, `acceptance.approverId` can never be set, and the Submit button's `isDisabled` check (`!acceptance.approverId`) permanently blocks submission. The risk acceptance workflow's request step is non-functional in production regardless of RR-002's authority-matrix filtering logic being correct, because the filtered list is always empty to begin with.

title: Frontend acceptance-status vocabulary ('draft'/'pending_approval') does not match the backend's real AcceptanceStatus enum ('not_applicable'/'pending'/'approved'/'rejected'/'expired') — the workflow UI renders no form at all for any risk sourced from the real backend
description: The backend's canonical `AcceptanceStatus` type is `'not_applicable' | 'pending' | 'approved' | 'rejected' | 'expired'` and every newly-created risk defaults to `acceptance.status: 'not_applicable'` (confirmed at risk.repository.ts:490 and ModuleRiskService.ts:476). `RiskAcceptanceWorkflow.jsx`'s render logic only shows `AcceptanceRequestForm` when `acceptance.status === 'draft'` and only shows `ApprovalDecisionForm` when `acceptance.status === 'pending_approval'` — neither of which is a real backend value. `submitAcceptanceRequest` in the repository sets the real status to `'pending'`, not `'pending_approval'`. The practical effect: for every risk loaded from the real API (status `'not_applicable'` before any request, or `'pending'` after a real request is submitted), none of this component's status checks match, so it renders nothing — no submit form, no approve/reject form. The component is only reachable via its own locally-optimistic state transitions (e.g. immediately after a client-side `handleSubmit`/`handleApprove` call before any reload), not against real persisted/reloaded data. This makes the entire risk-acceptance workflow UI non-functional for its primary purpose.

title: Auto-promoted compliance-coverage risks carry no structured link to the UCL control/requirement whose coverage degraded - only free text
description:
ComplianceCoverageRiskIntegrationService.handleCoverageDegraded (risk-management-service/src/services/ComplianceCoverageRiskIntegrationService.ts:60-93) has clientRequirementId, requirementCode, requirementTitle, frameworkId, frameworkName in hand, but only burns them into free-text title/description (lines 62, 107-127) and into an opaque sourceExternalId string - it never sets mappings.uclControls/mappings.frameworks on the risk it creates. BaseIntegrationService.createRiskFromEvent (BaseIntegrationService.ts:300) defaults mappings to empty arrays whenever the caller doesn't supply them. This is systemic across all 9 auto-promotion services: only VendorRiskIntegrationService.ts:467 sets mappings at all, and even that uses a stale field shape that doesn't match the current RiskMappings interface. Prowler, Evidence, Policy, Connector, Trust Vault, and Audit integration services never touch mappings.

Auditor-facing breakage: opening an auto-promoted risk (e.g. '[COMPLIANCE] Coverage degraded - Access Control Policy (ISO 27001)') gives a human-readable title but no clickable/structured pointer to the specific UCL control or client_requirements document - the real ID only survives inside a raw DB string field an auditor has no UI to inspect.

title: Risk evidence is siloed and one-directional; never feeds the linked control's evidence coverage dimension in /grc-framework
description:
Two separate evidence paths exist on a risk (RiskEvidencePanel.jsx): direct upload (lines 809-836) writes into risk-management-service's own RiskEvidence collection, S3-backed and entirely separate from vibrantix-backend's Evidence model - this evidence can never appear in /evidence-management, there is no shared record at all. Repository-linked evidence (lines 864-879) just appends an existing Evidence _id to risk.evidence[] via riskService.updateRisk - vibrantix-backend's evidence module has zero riskIds/linkedRisks field anywhere, so the Evidence document itself never learns it's referenced by a risk; viewing that same evidence item from /evidence-management shows no cross-reference back to the risk. Consequence for coverage scoring: recomputeCoverage (client-compliance-sync.service.js:1784) only pulls evidenceIds from ClientRequirement/ClientControl documents - never from a linked risk's own evidenceIds. RiskComplianceBridgeService only has event types for requirement/UCL mapping changes - none for evidence.

Auditor-facing breakage: evidence attached to a risk never contributes to that control's 'evidence' coverage dimension, even when the risk itself is correctly UCL-mapped, and is invisible from the evidence register entirely for the direct-upload path.

title: Coverage's 'risk' dimension is a flat existence flag blind to status/treatment - a fully-treated risk gets the same credit as an untreated one, and can leave a control 'uncovered' despite full remediation
description:
recomputeCoverage/recomputeControlCoverage score the risk dimension as binary: risk: (validated ? validated.riskDocs.length : riskIds.length) ? 100 : 0 (client-compliance-sync.service.js:1839, mirrored for controls at :2659). The underlying query (resource-hydration.util.js:196-204) filters only isArchived !== true - its own comment states every open phase AND the terminal closure phase still count as a real, currently-tracked risk. Weight is WEIGHTS.risk = 10 out of 100 (:1848). Both directions confirmed: an open, untreated risk contributes the exact same +10 'risk' credit as a fully treated/closed risk; a control whose only signal is a fully treated/closed risk, with no evidence/policy/vendor/trust attached, still scores 10/100 -> statusFromScore classifies it 'gap' - so a control can show 'uncovered' in /grc-framework even though its associated risk has been fully remediated. No event type exists for risk status/treatment/phase changes anywhere in the outbox.

Auditor-facing breakage: an auditor cannot tell from the coverage view whether a linked risk is still live or resolved, and remediated risks can paradoxically make a control look worse (still 'gap') than one with no risk history at all once other dimensions are weak.
requirement: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 8.3 risk treatment implementation; ISO/IEC 27007:2019 §6.3.2
